rules.definition: uses financial jargon or acronyms (APY, APR, FDIC, CD, compounding, variable rate, yield)
rules.rule: When a wording adds jargon, synthetic appeal drops by about 0.9 points (90% CI -1.2 to -0.7; 5 variants, 5 concepts).
rules.advice: Concepts that depend on jargon are fragile; reword without it or test in market.

rules.definition: sells by saying what is NOT there (no fees, never, zero, without, don't)
rules.rule: When a wording adds negation, synthetic appeal drops by about 0.4 points (90% CI -0.6 to -0.2; 5 variants, 4 concepts).
rules.advice: Concepts that depend on negation are fragile; reword without it or test in market.

rules.definition: frames the offer as avoiding a loss (stop losing, don't let X eat, miss out, before it's gone)
rules.rule: When a wording adds loss frame, synthetic appeal drops by about 0.7 points (90% CI -0.8 to -0.6; 17 variants, 16 concepts).
rules.advice: Concepts that depend on loss frame are fragile; reword without it or test in market.

rules.definition: contains three or more separate numbers or percentages
pressures the reader on time (today, now, limited time, act now, before rates drop)
